text:
liam: heads up — us-west-2 gpu pool is at 98% GPU utilization and queue depth spiked 4x around 16:12. seeing timeouts for heavy-generation routes (gpt-rlhf-16k).
ops-bot: ALERT: cluster/us-west-2/gpu-pool-3: queue_depth=745, avg_latency=820ms, gpu_util=98% :warning:
maya: confirmed. admission control kicked in for several internal customers. some requests are being queued >5s.
jess: are we spilling to other regions automatically? last config said cross-region spillover=enabled but only for low-priority tenants.
andrew: currently policy: if queue_depth > 500 and latency > 700ms -> attempt spill to same-model in nearest region with capacity, else try model-fallback to quantized variant. but routing is also bounded by per-tenant cost caps so some bursts are blocked.
liam: what are the candidate regions for spill? us-east-1 and eu-west-1? network egress for some customers will balloon.
raman: correct — primary targets: us-east-1, eu-west-1. network egress delta estimate ~0.8–1.2c/token depending on path. that matters for customers on usage billing.
maya: quick idea — prefer model-fallback to gpu-quantized-8bit in-region for high-SLA customers, spill to another region for best-effort. need a deterministic tiering: Tier A = no spill, fallback only; Tier B = allow spill to same continent; Tier C = global spill allowed.
jess: love that. how do we implement deterministically? customer metadata + route config?
andrew: can add a new routing policy field: "saturation_policy": {"tier": "A|B|C", "fallback_order": ["in-region-quant", "regional-spill", "global-spill"]}. simple feature flag on rollout.
liam: while we decide policy, can we flip to immediate model-fallback globally for this pool to relieve pressure? what's the quick command?
maya: run this on control plane: 
```
POST /admin/routing/pools/us-west-2/gpu-pool-3/actions
{ "action": "force_fallback", "target_variant": "gpt-rlhf-16k-8bit", "percent": 100 }
```
That will route new requests to the 8bit variant in-region. latency should drop and free KV cache pressure.
ops-bot: ACTION: routing override deployed by maya — force_fallback->gpt-rlhf-16k-8bit (100%) on pool gpu-pool-3.
raman: monitoring shows queue depth down to 410 after 90s. avg_latency 420ms. still ~200 requests in flight. cost delta estimate: +6% for some customers due to 8bit model throughput change but less cross-region egress.
jess: we should communicate to account teams: Tier A customers experienced brief impact but we avoided cross-region egress. can we capture which tenants had requests dropped vs queued?
andrew: logs are in s3: s3://redwood-ops/alerts/us-west-2/1752981123/*. use this query to get dropped requests: 
```
select tenant_id, count(*) from request_events
where pool='gpu-pool-3' and event in ('dropped','timed_out') and ts between 1752981000 and 1752982200
group by tenant_id
order by count desc
limit 50;
```
liam: perfect. also put a temp admission control tweak: reduce max_concurrent_per_tenant by 20% for non-exempt tenants. command?
maya: run: 
```
PATCH /admin/tenants/admission
{ "selector": "!exempt", "max_concurrent_delta_pct": -20 }
```
That should shed hotspots fast.
raman: small caveat — some background batch jobs are marked non-exempt and will retry continuously. we might push them into scheduled windows instead.
jess: can we add an emergency routing rule that prefers in-region quantized but preserves model quality checks for top 20% customers? We don't want quality regressions.
andrew: yes — add a canary rule: route 100% of Tier A to fallback only if quality monitoring (evals) shows <2% regression on the slice. otherwise route 50/50 and fallback to spill when quality rules pass. We can codify as: 
```
"canary_quality_gate": {
  "metric": "delta_perplexity",
  "threshold": 0.02,
  "window_sec": 600
}
```
liam: good. action items: 1) send note to accounts (jess) 2) run tenant drop query (andrew) 3) keep fallback override active until queue <200 for 10m (maya) 4) propose saturation_policy RFC tomorrow (liam & andrew).
maya: I'll also add a telemetry dashboard for "spill_egress_cost_estimate" per customer so sales can see potential billing impact.
ops-bot: RESOLVED: queue_depth normalized to 180 at 1752982230. fallback override remains for 10m cooldown.
jess: I'll draft the account message now and ping PMs.
liam: thanks all — we'll reconvene after the RFC tomorrow.
